question: Record retention period for Delhi Police control-room audio, wireless logs and CCTV.
why_it_matters: Once destroyed under a lawful schedule the RTI reply is a truthful 'not available'. Filing on day 40 gets nothing that filing on day 25 would have got.
lawful_route: RTI for the retention schedule itself, which is a record.

question: Record retention period for Bihar Police control-room audio, wireless logs and CCTV at Patna, Katihar and Munger.
why_it_matters: No preservation order is known for Bihar, so nothing is currently interrupting any schedule.
lawful_route: RTI for the retention schedule; and a written preservation representation to SSP Patna, SP Katihar, SP Munger.

question: What is 'the SOP in place' referred to in the Delhi High Court's preservation direction, and what does it cover?
why_it_matters: It determines what was actually required to be preserved.
lawful_route: RTI to Delhi Police via rtionline.gov.in; and the order text from the High Court site.

question: The text of the Delhi High Court order of 22 July 2026 in W.P.(CRL) 2127/2026, and which petitions were heard with it.
why_it_matters: Partly answered on 18 August 2026: the cause title, case number, listing date and bench are now established from the court's own cause list (PROC-DEL-002). What is still unheld is the order itself. Every statement this archive makes about what the court directed (preservation of CCTV footage and videography, four weeks for a counter affidavit, the 11 September listing) rests on news reports of a document that is public and free. ANSWERED 18 September 2026: the order was retrieved from the court's own portal and is at PROC-DEL-004. The answer was not the expected one. The order dismisses the petition and contains none of the directions the news reports attributed to it, so PROC-DEL-001 moves to DISPUTED and OQ-051 opens.
lawful_route: Delhi High Court order PDFs are served directly at delhihighcourt.nic.in/app/showFileJudgment/<filename>.pdf and can be downloaded without a login once the filename is known: an order in another matter was retrieved that way on 18 August 2026 to confirm it. The filename is assigned by the registry and is not derivable, so it has to come from the case-status or judgment search, both of which sit behind a captcha and need a person. Cause lists, by contrast, are directly downloadable: combined_cause_list_DD.MM.YYYY.pdf and rlDDMMYYYY.pdf under delhihighcourt.nic.in/files/YYYY-MM/cause-list/. The 11 September 2026 listing is the next opportunity to capture the order and the connected matters in one go.

question: The report published by The Hindu on 20 July 2026 on which the NHRC founded its cognisance.
why_it_matters: Three outlets attribute the NHRC's action to it. It is the founding document of the oversight proceeding.
lawful_route: Publisher archive or library.

question: PIO designations for every office in the document custody category, in all three jurisdictions.
why_it_matters: The entire custody section is UNKNOWN without them. No RTI can be correctly addressed.
lawful_route: s.4(1)(b) RTI Act proactive disclosure, which is published and requires no application.

question: Bihar RTI Rules: application fee, appeal fee, per-page copying charge, inspection charge.
why_it_matters: Union and Maharashtra figures must not be carried across.
lawful_route: Bihar gazette or the Jaankari portal's rules page.

question: Are SP Katihar, SP Munger and the relevant Patna police authority enrolled as PIOs on Jaankari, or is postal filing required?
why_it_matters: Determines the filing mechanism for three of the four Bihar incidents.
lawful_route: Jaankari portal PIO directory.

question: Does any binding Supreme Court or NHRC guideline address the use of force against assemblies specifically, as distinct from custody and encounter deaths?
why_it_matters: If none exists, that gap may be the most substantively important thing this archive can document. It is also the claim most likely to be wrong through a failure to search well.
lawful_route: Supreme Court judgment search; NHRC guidelines and annual reports.

question: Are the Delhi, Bihar and Maharashtra police manuals published, partially published, or RTI-only?
why_it_matters: The manual is where crowd-control procedure actually lives.
lawful_route: State police and home department websites; RTI if not published.

question: Full operative text of BNSS ss.148 to 151 compared word for word against the gazette.
why_it_matters: Section numbers and headings are verified across three sources; the operative text is not.
lawful_route: India Code BNSS PDF, already held.

question: BNSS s.196 verified against India Code.
why_it_matters: Currently REPORTED only.
lawful_route: India Code.

question: Is the Bihar Police Act 2007 Bihar Act 1 of 2007 or Bihar Act 7 of 2007?
why_it_matters: Two sources conflict. The act number cannot be cited until resolved.
lawful_route: Bihar gazette.

question: Correct citations and text of PUCL v. State of Maharashtra and D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal.
why_it_matters: Currently held from a single secondary source and unread.
lawful_route: Supreme Court website.

question: Does any state police statute contain a command responsibility provision?
why_it_matters: Chain of authority is the archive's central question and no statutory hook has been found.
lawful_route: India Code full-text search of the three acts.

question: CIC position on OCI cardholders and foreign nationals under s.3 RTI Act.
why_it_matters: Determines whether two of the four filer scenarios have any RTI route at all.
lawful_route: CIC published decisions.

question: Do any of the three payment gateways accept a foreign-issued card? Does HRCNet OTP accept a foreign mobile number?
why_it_matters: Determines whether a non-resident can file without a resident co-filer, and therefore whether the exposure risk at OQ-025 is avoidable.
lawful_route: Direct test, or portal helpdesk.

question: Record access regimes at the Delhi, Patna and Bombay High Courts and the Supreme Court.
why_it_matters: Determines cost and method for every court document in the archive.
lawful_route: Each court's own rules and Registry pages.

question: Current official Delhi Police View FIR URL.
why_it_matters: Do not construct one by editing a path.
lawful_route: delhipolice.gov.in navigation.

question: Were FIRs registered against protesters, against police, or both, in any of the four incidents, and what are their numbers?
why_it_matters: FIR numbers are the key into the eCourts case search.
lawful_route: scrb.bihar.gov.in for Bihar; Delhi Police View FIR once OQ-019 resolves.

question: NHRC diary or case numbers for the suo motu proceeding and the Vashisht complaint; and whether the Delhi Police report called for on 25 July has been filed.
why_it_matters: The Diary or Case Number is the citation handle for a pending case.
lawful_route: HRCNet public complaint search.

question: Is a report submitted by a police authority to a human rights commission reachable by RTI against the commission, against the force, or neither?
why_it_matters: Determines whether the central oversight documents ever become accessible.
lawful_route: RTI to both, and CIC decisions on the point.

question: Notice periods and tabling procedure for questions in all four houses, and session calendars for the coming year.
why_it_matters: Determines whether the legislature route is usable within the archive's timeframe.
lawful_route: Each House's Rules of Procedure, linked from its own site.

question: Identity, date and location of the Maharashtra incident.
why_it_matters: Determines jurisdiction, public authority, eCourts establishment, and High Court bench.
lawful_route: Held at the archive operator's instruction pending their identification.

question: If a resident co-filer is used to solve a citizenship or payment problem, how is their exposure under s.11 RTI Act managed?
why_it_matters: The co-filer's name and address go on the application and may be disclosed to the third party whose records are sought.
lawful_route: Not a research task. A decision for the archive operator before any co-filed application.

question: Any documented instance of an Indian accountability archive facing a takedown, suit, criminal complaint, or source exposure.
why_it_matters: Determines what defensive posture this archive needs.
lawful_route: Legal press; digital rights organisations.

question: Who operates delhi-police-violence.vercel.app, on what verification method, and is it durable?
why_it_matters: An anonymous parallel archive is either a collaborator or a liability and cannot be cited until known.
lawful_route: Site metadata; direct contact.

question: Is 'Cockroach Janta Party' the organisation's actual registered or self-adopted name?
why_it_matters: It must not enter the archive as a proper noun on tertiary sourcing alone.
lawful_route: Primary court filings, which name parties.

question: Are armoury issue registers exempt under s.8 RTI Act, and on what ground?
why_it_matters: Determines whether the equipment-issue chain is reachable at all.
lawful_route: File and see; CIC decisions on analogous records.

question: Was a magisterial inquiry ordered for any of the four incidents?
why_it_matters: BNSS s.196 is triggered by death, disappearance or custodial rape only. Do not assume one exists. 'No inquiry ordered' is a finding.
lawful_route: RTI to the District Magistrate in each district.

question: The Delhi Police affidavit filed in W.P.(Crl.) 280/2026 concerning the use of facial recognition technology at the Jantar Mantar protest.
why_it_matters: It is the force's own account of what it deployed against a protest, sworn to a court. Everything this archive says about the deployment currently rests on reports of it. An affidavit also fixes who swore it, which is the closest the record has come to a named official taking responsibility for anything at Jantar Mantar.
lawful_route: Supreme Court case status and filings for W.P.(Crl.) 280/2026 at sci.gov.in; the SCR portal at scr.sci.gov.in for orders; and, once a diary number is known, a certified copy from the registry. Parties' counsel are on the record and the pleadings are public documents in a public interest matter.

question: Which database of photographs the facial recognition system matched against at Jantar Mantar, who supplied it, and whether any private company processed the data.
why_it_matters: A facial recognition match requires an underlying set of photographs of citizens. Delhi Police is reported to have named a 'Crime Kundli' database and dossier records; the petitioners allege a private company processed the data. Neither the composition of the database nor its lawful basis is established, and a face captured at a protest that matches nothing is still a face that was captured.
lawful_route: RTI to the Commissioner of Police, Delhi, for the sanction, procurement record and standard operating procedure for the facial recognition system, and for any contract with a processor. Note a documented precedent from a different event: a certified copy of Election Commission of India letter No. 23/SEC/2020-ERS dated 12 March 2020, from the Under Secretary to the Chief Electoral Officer, NCT of Delhi, records that the Commission declined to share the electoral database of an entire district with police but directed the CEO to display the electoral roll with elector images of North-East Parliamentary Constituency before investigating officials, on Delhi Police's request to match elector photographs against CCTV images. That letter concerns only the 2020 violence in Delhi and is a lead on how such a database can be assembled; it offers no evidence about Jantar Mantar or these incidents. It was seen only as a photograph circulated online and should be obtained from the Commission or the CEO before being relied on.

question: Who authorised an AK-47, described by the State as a platoon-level weapon for special operations, to be carried on law-and-order duty at a student protest at Siwan on 25 July 2026.
why_it_matters: This is the archive's question in its purest form, and the State has opened the door to it by admitting the weapon should not have been there. Somebody decided the deployment, drew the weapon from an armoury and recorded the issue. Arms issue registers, deployment orders and the daily diary are records, and they are the kind of record that answers who gave the order.
lawful_route: RTI to the Superintendent of Police, Siwan, and to the District Magistrate, Siwan, for the deployment order for 25 July 2026, the arms and ammunition issue register entry, the daily diary entries for the relevant hours, and any requisition of armed force. Separately, the suspension order and the departmental proceeding record for the named constable. File before any retention period runs: no court is known to have ordered preservation in Bihar.

question: How many police personnel were injured at Jantar Mantar on 20 July 2026, and over what period the figure is counted.
why_it_matters: Delhi Police told the Supreme Court more than 240 were injured. Earlier reporting of the same events gives 118. The archive cannot hold both as the count for the same day, and the difference is not a detail: the injury figures on both sides are what the proportionality of the force will be argued from.
lawful_route: The affidavit itself will state the period and the basis. Medico-legal case records are held by the hospitals that treated the injured and are obtainable in aggregate by RTI without identifying anyone. The same request should cover protester injuries, which are separately contested.

question: The medico-legal records and treatment of the three protesters reported to have sustained firearm injuries at Siwan, and whether any FIR records the firing.
why_it_matters: Three people were shot at a protest, on the State's own account. Whether that was recorded as an offence, investigated, or treated only as a departmental matter against one constable is the difference between an incident and a case.
lawful_route: RTI to the Superintendent of Police, Siwan, for FIRs registered in connection with the events of 25 July 2026 including any registered on the firing itself; and to the civil surgeon, Siwan, for the number of medico-legal cases arising that day. Do not seek anything that would identify an injured person.

question: The Delhi Government (Home Department) order of 18 August 2026 transferring 43 IPS and DANIPS officers, and any file noting recording the reason for the two postings reported as connected to the Jantar Mantar policing.
why_it_matters: The order is the only document that could show whether the two moves had anything to do with the protest, and reporting says on its face it does not. Either answer is worth having: a routine rejig closes a line of speculation, and a noting that says otherwise is the first record of an office acting on the police action.
lawful_route: Transfer and posting orders of this kind are ordinarily published by the Home Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, on delhi.gov.in. If it is not there, RTI to the Public Information Officer, Home Department, GNCTD, for the order dated 18 August 2026 and the Police Establishment Board recommendation behind it. Ask for the order.

question: Which database the facial recognition at Jantar Mantar matched faces against, which body supplied the images in it, and under what authority they were shared.
why_it_matters: Delhi Police has admitted the deployment and says it matched only against crime records. A matching system needs a set of images to match against, and where that set came from is an authorisation question of exactly the kind this archive exists to ask. Nothing on the record answers it. Saket Gokhale, a Trinamool Congress leader and former Rajya Sabha member, publicly put the same question to the Election Commission, UIDAI, the Income Tax Department, the Transport Department and Delhi Police in August 2026, and has separately obtained hospital records on the pellet injuries by Right to Information (INC-DEL-006); no reply from any of them is on this record, and a question asked in public is not an answer.
lawful_route: RTI to the Public Information Officer, Delhi Police, for the name of the database or databases used for facial recognition at Jantar Mantar in July 2026 and for any memorandum of understanding or data-sharing arrangement under which images were obtained; and to the Election Commission of India and the NCRB for any arrangement to share photographic records with Delhi Police that was in force in July 2026. Ask for documents and dates. The disclosure sought in PROC-SC-007 covers the same ground and may answer it first.

question: Delhi Police General Diary entry 0008A of 22 July 2026, Parliament Street police station, recording the munitions used at Jantar Mantar on 20 July 2026 and the Deputy Commissioner of Police under whose orders they were used.
why_it_matters: Two outlets report having read it and this archive has not. It is the only document described anywhere that ties the use of force at Jantar Mantar to an officer who ordered it, and it is a routine police record. Holding it would move the archive from reporting what a newspaper says a record says to holding the record.
lawful_route: RTI to the Public Information Officer, Delhi Police, for a copy of General Diary entry 0008A dated 22 July 2026 of Parliament Street police station. Ask for the entry by its number and date. If exemption is claimed under section 8, the refusal is itself a record worth publishing and opens a first appeal. The same entry may be produced in W.P.(C) 917/2026, in which case the court record is the better route.

question: The Delhi Police standard operating procedure on the use of pellet-firing weapons, which the Supreme Court is reported to have directed be placed on record on 30 July 2026.
why_it_matters: Either it exists and authorises these weapons, or it exists and does not mention them, or there is none. All three answers are findings, and counsel has told the Court there is no such standing order at all. This is the document the archive was built to ask for.
lawful_route: Watch the record in Yashovardhan Azad and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors., W.P.(C) 917/2026 for the affidavit filing it. In parallel, RTI to the Public Information Officer, Delhi Police, for any standing order, SOP or circular governing the use of pellet-firing or anti-riot guns. Ask for the document and do not ask for confirmation that none exists. A nil reply is only useful if the question was framed so that a nil reply means something.

question: The ammunition log of the Rapid Action Force unit deployed at Jantar Mantar on 20 July 2026, which the Supreme Court is reported to have directed be preserved on 30 July 2026.
why_it_matters: An ammunition log records what was issued and what was returned. Against the General Diary entry it is the check on whether the reported two rounds of plastic pellets is the whole of it. It is marked time critical because logs are subject to routine destruction schedules and a preservation direction is only as good as somebody asking for the thing later.
lawful_route: The Rapid Action Force is a unit of the Central Reserve Police Force, so the application goes to the Public Information Officer, CRPF; Delhi Police is the wrong office for it. Cite the reported preservation direction of 30 July 2026 in W.P.(C) 917/2026 by date and case number, which forecloses any answer that the record has been weeded.

question: Which Deputy Commissioner of Police gave the order recorded in General Diary entry 0008A, and whether that order was written or oral.
why_it_matters: This is the question the site is named after, narrowed for the first time to a rank, a date and a police record that is said to name the office. Everything else in this archive asks who authorised the use of force in general terms. This asks it of one entry in one diary.
lawful_route: It follows OQ-040: obtain the entry first, since it is reported to record the office. Alt News says it is withholding the officers' names, so the names are in the document. If the entry records an oral order, the wireless log and the control room recording for 20 July become the next request, and both are subject to short retention periods.

question: The standard operating procedure prepared in 2011 by a Union High Task Force on crowd control, and the report of the High Powered Committee of 2016, which counsel told the Supreme Court is not available.
why_it_matters: If a national protocol on these weapons was written in 2011 and reviewed in 2016, then what any force may lawfully do is a buried question. A report that a party's counsel could not obtain is worth obtaining.
lawful_route: RTI to the Ministry of Home Affairs for the 2011 standard operating procedure and for the report of the High Powered Committee of 2016, by name and year. Also worth checking the Bureau of Police Research and Development, which publishes work of this kind. This is a records request about policy documents and touches no individual.

question: The Supreme Court's order of 18 August 2026 constituting the High Powered Enquiry Committee, and the committee's terms of reference as issued.
why_it_matters: The committee's mandate is reported to include the deployment of pellet guns by name. What it may and may not examine, what powers it has and what it must report on are all fixed by the order, and this archive holds only journalists' accounts of it. The order is also the document that would settle whether this matter is a civil or a criminal writ, which the reporting cites both ways. PARTLY INFORMED 14 October 2026: the Committee's own site states the mandate and the priority paragraphs (PROC-SC-016). The order itself is still unheld; the site links it at hpec.nic.in/supreme-court-orders. ANSWERED 14 October 2026: the order of 18 August 2026 was supplied and read in full, and is at PROC-SC-018. The Committee's mandate, powers and reporting duty are fixed by paragraphs 12 to 27 of that order. The caption shows the lead matter as a criminal writ petition, W.P.(Crl.) No. 280/2026, with civil writ petitions connected.
lawful_route: Supreme Court orders are published on the Court's own site and are free. Retrieve it by case number and date of order and record the URL actually fetched. Do not reconstruct a path. If the number is wrong, search the cause list for 10 September 2026, the reported next date.

question: The First Information Report registered at Parliament Street police station on 21 August 2026 on the complaint of a student injured at Jantar Mantar: its number, the sections invoked, and who it names.
why_it_matters: It is the first criminal case in this archive about the police action. The sections invoked will show whether it is being investigated as an offence by identified persons or as an incident by persons unknown, and an FIR against unidentified persons can stay that way indefinitely unless somebody is watching.
lawful_route: FIRs are required to be published online within a fixed period (CRT-006), and the Delhi Police publication route is recorded as UNKNOWN (CRT-005), so establishing that route is the first step and is useful well beyond this FIR. Failing that, RTI to the Public Information Officer, Delhi Police, for FIRs registered at Parliament Street police station on 21 August 2026. Ask by station and date.

question: Copies of the Right to Information replies from Lady Hardinge Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital recording pellet or projectile injuries treated on 20 July 2026.
why_it_matters: This is the shortest path from CORROBORATED to VERIFIED anywhere in the archive. The replies exist, an identified person holds them, and every outlet that reported them worked from the same two documents without reproducing either. Holding the replies would mean the archive was reading the hospitals.
lawful_route: Two routes, and the first is a courtesy that rests on no statute: ask Saket Gokhale, who obtained them and has publicised them, for copies. Failing that, file the same applications directly with the Public Information Officers of Lady Hardinge Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, asking only for the number of persons treated for pellet, shot or projectile injuries on 20 July 2026. Ask for a number. Do not ask for anything that identifies a patient, both because it is wrong and because it invites the refusal recorded at OVR-DEL-002.

question: The AIIMS refusal letter of about 20 August 2026, whether a first appeal was filed against it, and the reply from Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital.
why_it_matters: Two hospitals answered a question the third refused, so the refusal is testable. It is marked time critical because a first appeal under section 19(1) must be filed within thirty days of the refusal and that window closes in the second half of September 2026. If no appeal is filed the refusal simply stands, and the count of people treated at the largest hospital in the group is never established.
lawful_route: The appeal is the applicant's to file and this project cannot file it for him. What this project can do is ask AIIMS the same question itself, which restarts a clock of its own and produces either the number or a second refusal on the same ground, and either outcome is a record. RML can be asked directly for the reply that was never sent. Ask for numbers only.

question: The fact-finding report of the PUCL Bihar public hearing of 22 August 2026, as a document.
why_it_matters: It is the only sustained account of the Bihar police action that does not come from the State of Bihar, and it names its panel, which means it can be weighed. Three outlets have described it and none has published it. A report that exists and cannot be read is a gap this archive can close by asking.
lawful_route: Write to the People's Union for Civil Liberties, Bihar unit, and ask for the report and any annexures. This is a non-statutory request to a civil society organisation for its own published work, and it should be made as one: say what the archive is, say that the report would be indexed and attributed to PUCL, and say that testimony identifying individuals will not be republished.

question: The 64 FIRs said to have been registered in connection with the Bihar student protests of July 2026, and whether any records police action at Sitamarhi on 21 July.
why_it_matters: Sixty-four FIRs is a specific number from a named panel and nothing else on this record corroborates it. The FIRs would also settle whether Sitamarhi belongs in this archive as its own incident, which currently rests on a single account.
lawful_route: Bihar Police publish FIRs at scrb.bihar.gov.in and CRT-003 records that the State Crime Records Bureau says all FIRs are published there. Search by district and date range for Patna, Siwan and Sitamarhi between 21 and 27 July 2026. That is a public database and needs no application.

question: The advisory on handling protests circulated to Delhi Police personnel after 20 July 2026: the document, who issued it, on what date, and whether any instruction on the use of force or crowd-control weapons was issued alongside it.
why_it_matters: A written instruction to a police force about protests, circulated to 15 districts, is exactly the class of document this archive exists to obtain. As reported it is about how officers appear on camera and says nothing about weapons. The archive has not read it, and the second half of the question is the important one.
lawful_route: RTI to the Public Information Officer, Delhi Police, for any circular, advisory or standing instruction on the handling of public assemblies issued on or after 20 July 2026, and for any instruction on the use of force or crowd-control equipment issued in the same period. Ask for both in one application so that producing the first and withholding the second is a visible choice.

question: The armoury issue and return registers for the police units deployed at Siwan on 25 July 2026, and any ballistics or forensic examination of the rounds fired.
why_it_matters: The State says four AK-47 rounds at one location. An open-source investigation says at least nine at two others. An issue and return register settles how many rounds left the armoury and how many came back, and it does so without anybody's account being believed. It is marked time critical because these registers are working documents on ordinary retention schedules and nobody has been reported to have asked for them.
lawful_route: RTI to the Public Information Officer, Superintendent of Police, Siwan, for the armoury issue and return register entries for 25 July 2026 and for any forensic or ballistics report on rounds recovered. Ask for the register entries. If exemption is claimed, the ground is itself worth publishing.

question: In which proceeding, if any, did the Delhi High Court direct preservation of CCTV footage and videography in relation to the 20 and 21 July 2026 police action, and what does that order say?
why_it_matters: Four news reports place that direction in W.P.(CRL) 2127/2026. The order in that case, now held at PROC-DEL-004, dismisses the petition and directs nothing. Either a preservation direction exists in a matter this archive has not identified, or it does not exist. The difference decides whether anything currently interrupts the retention schedule for the Delhi footage, and the archive is presently unable to say which.
lawful_route: The combined cause list for 22 July 2026 is already held (PROC-DEL-002) and lists every matter before the same bench that day; the connected numbers the order itself names, LPA 539/2026 and W.P.(C) 9770/2026, are a second route. Both are free. Case status at delhihighcourt.nic.in/app/get-case-type-status takes the literal case type string and returns an order list per case; PROC-DEL-004 records how.

question: Were any of the July 2026 telecommunications suspension orders for Central Delhi published, and if so where; and does the confidential witness portal directed by the Supreme Court on 10 September 2026 now exist, at what address?
why_it_matters: Two halves of the same problem. CUS-SHUT-001 records the Internet Freedom Foundation's observation on 20 July that no suspension order had been published; this archive has not itself searched every gazette and portal, so it records that as reported. An absence is the hardest thing to prove and the easiest to assert. The portal matters for a different reason: it is the one route this archive could point a frightened witness to, and pointing anyone at a portal whose existence is unconfirmed would be worse than saying nothing. PARTLY ANSWERED 14 October 2026: the Committee's own site, hpec.nic.in, advertises a confidential route for vulnerable witnesses and names a Member Secretary (PROC-SC-017). Whether the route works has not been tested, and the second-order question of whether it is the portal the Court directed is an inference. The telecommunications-suspension half is unchanged. The order of 10 September, now held (PROC-SC-019), says only that a portal 'may be created'. It directs nothing and names no address. So the portal half rests on the Committee's own site (PROC-SC-017) and on whether that route works.
lawful_route: Search the MHA, DoT, GNCTD and Delhi Police sites; FQ-014 for the orders; FQ-016 for the order copy.

question: Which office issued the section 163 BNSS order in force across New Delhi district on 2 October 2026, on what date, covering what area and hours, and what does its text say?
why_it_matters: The sources split on whether Delhi Police or the Delhi government issued it (INC-DEL-013), and the two answers lead to different custodians. Unlike a lathi charge, a prohibitory order is a written instrument with a date, a signatory and a stated ground, so this is a question a document can answer. No copy has been found. Siasat reports that security personnel told protesters on 7 October that section 163 was in force (INC-DEL-024). Whether that is the order of 2 October extended or a new one is not established, and the sources read do not say how long the order ran.
lawful_route: FQ-020. The route differs by custodian: Delhi Police uses the Union RTI portal; this archive has not established the Delhi government route.

question: Was an order suspending mobile internet made for the Jantar Mantar area on 2 October 2026, by which office, under which power, and was it reviewed?
why_it_matters: One outlet reports a suspension of several hours (INC-DEL-015). If an order exists it should be public under the Supreme Court's direction in Anuradha Bhasin, and its absence from public view would itself be recordable.
lawful_route: FQ-021, built on the same lines as FQ-014 for the July order.

question: What is the status of the three FIRs reported over the 2 October 2026 protest, at which police stations, against whom, and has any FIR been registered on the journalist's complaint or on the three complaints sent to the Crime Branch?
why_it_matters: The only source (INC-DEL-016) says no accused was named in any of the three FIRs, and quotes the Cockroach Janta Party as saying police will not register one against the officer the journalist named. That is one outlet, one day after the event, and it can change daily. This archive has not found where, or whether, Delhi Police publishes registered FIRs, and does not name a portal it has not seen. PTI and Deccan Chronicle report on 4 October that no FIR was registered when the three journalists went to a station and that the complaints went to the Crime Branch (INC-DEL-022). Three FIRs over the protest itself are recorded at INC-DEL-017.
lawful_route: No route established for Delhi. Establish the publication route first; an RTI application is the fallback.

question: Who is named in the Shivaji Park FIR of 3 October 2026, and was it registered on a private complaint or on the police's own motion?
why_it_matters: Three outlets give three different lists of names and two different accounts of the complainant (INC-MAH-004). A private complaint and a police-initiated case sit with different offices.
lawful_route: FQ-022: the FIR itself.

question: Was the refusal of permission for the Shivaji Park gathering of 2 October 2026 given in writing, on what date, by which office and signatory, and on what stated ground?
why_it_matters: All three sources say permission was refused and one gives a Bombay High Court judgment and a government order as the ground (INC-MAH-003). The refusal is a written instrument that can be asked for by name, which is the thing this archive cannot get for a baton.
lawful_route: FQ-022. Maharashtra's rules allow one subject matter per application, so the refusal and the FIR go in separately.

question: Was force used on 2 October 2026 beyond moving people onto buses, and does footage, a medical record or a police account exist that settles the allegation of beating with batons?
why_it_matters: The allegation rests on one outlet reporting what protesters said (INC-DEL-014). The retention period for CCTV covering the area is not established (RET-002), so any footage may be overwritten on a schedule nobody here knows. No preservation request has been drafted for 2 October: the four on this site cover Bihar and July.
lawful_route: A written preservation request to the office that holds the footage, and a medico-legal record request where a named person consents. The custodian for 2 October has not been established.

question: Who signed the Delhi Police order of 1 October 2026 refusing the Indian Youth Congress permission to demonstrate at Jantar Mantar, and what ground does it state?
why_it_matters: The order is reported by Bar and Bench (INC-DEL-020) and challenged in the Delhi High Court (PROC-DEL-005), so a copy sits in a court file. It is the Delhi counterpart of the written refusals at Mumbai and Kochi, and a refusal is a written instrument with an author.
lawful_route: FQ-023: the petition and its annexures from the Delhi High Court.

question: Was an FIR registered against Rahul Gandhi over the protest of 6 October 2026, at which police station, under which sections, and on whose complaint?
why_it_matters: Siasat mentions the FIR without describing it (INC-DEL-026). An FIR against the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a written instrument with a station, sections and a complainant, and one search result gave a different account of what it alleges that the page read does not support. The FIR settles it. No route to Delhi Police FIRs has been established by this archive.
lawful_route: Establish the publication route first; an RTI application is the fallback.

question: What did the Supreme Court do on 9 October 2026, the date the 10 September order listed W.P.(Crl.) No. 280/2026 and connected matters for further consideration, and has the Committee filed or been asked for a first interim report?
why_it_matters: The Committee's first report on issues (i) and (vi) of paragraph 12 was requested 'at the earliest' on 18 August and again on 10 September. The 9 October listing is the next point at which the Court could set a date for it, say anything about the confidential portal, or deal with the Delhi Police status report on the protection of the 14-year-old protester ordered in W.P.(C) No. 324/2026. No order of that date is held and no report of it has been found. SEARCHED 14 October 2026: a general search for the Supreme Court's 9 October hearing, the first interim report or any HPEC statement found nothing dated after the 10 September order. Absence from a news search is weak evidence. The order itself will be on the Committee's Supreme Court Orders page. 15 October 2026: the Supreme Court did hear a separate petition on 9 October (M A Baby v. Union of India, PROC-SC-020), on Metro and train closures and an alternative protest site. That is not the Tripathi batch (W.P.(Crl.) 280/2026), so this question remains open. 19 October 2026: the Supreme Court heard the contempt petitions on 11 and 15 October (PROC-SC-022), a different batch; the 9 October listing of W.P.(Crl.) 280/2026 is still not found.
lawful_route: The order of 9 October will appear on the Supreme Court's site and, as the two earlier orders did, on the Committee's Supreme Court Orders page (hpec.nic.in/supreme-court-orders). The archive owner can save it from there, the way the earlier two arrived.

question: The Delhi Police Commissioner's standing order of 11 October 2026 de-notifying Jantar Mantar as a protest site: its text, its date of issue and publication, the legal power it cites, the three replacement venues, and the revised SOP for protests said to follow. And the Ministry of Home Affairs committee on alternative venues that the order is reported to rest on: the order constituting it, its members, its terms of reference, its date and its recommendation.
why_it_matters: A written order from a named office removed the capital's designated protest site, and the police justify it by a Supreme Court order of 9 October that, as reported, only asks authorities to consider a site with basic amenities. Whether the standing order cites the Court's words accurately, under which statute it was made, whether it was published, and when it took effect (11 October, 12 October or 13 October, all of which appear in reporting) cannot be answered from news accounts. The SOP for the three new venues will govern the next protest. ThePrint quotes the standing order as resting on a Home Ministry committee's recommendations, while counsel told the High Court the step followed the Supreme Court's order of 9 October. A committee that recommended removing the capital's main protest site is a body with a constitution order and a report, both of which should exist on paper. 19 October 2026: the order is numbered L&O/48/2026 and is under challenge in Swaty Singh v. Union of India, W.P.(C) 1357/2026, where the Supreme Court issued notice on 15 October (PROC-SC-023); the Solicitor General told the Court a committee had reported with recorded reasons. The text, publication and committee order are still not held. SEARCHED 19 October 2026: no copy of the standing order was found online. Business Standard (12 Oct, seen only as a search summary because the page returned 403) quotes the order as saying the Home Ministry's committee on alternative venues recommended the de-notification. It puts Ramlila Maidan 3 km, CBD Ground 12 km and Burari Ground 23 km from Jantar Mantar. Bar and Bench (15 Oct) says Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court on 13 October that the decision rested on the Supreme Court's order of 9 October, and that the Centre has denied this.
lawful_route: The order and any SOP should be requested from Delhi Police by RTI through the rtionline.gov.in portal (see the Delhi Police entry in the authority list), and checked against Delhi Police's own website. The Delhi High Court file in the Indian Youth Congress matter (PROC-DEL-005, FQ-023) may carry it as an annexure, and the police are likely to place it before the Supreme Court if the application there is heard. The Home Ministry's committee order and report can be requested from the Ministry of Home Affairs through rtionline.gov.in.

question: Which State Government notification under BNSS s.15 designates the Delhi Police officers (reported as ACP rank) who heard the CJP leaders' preventive cases on 11, 14, 17 and 18 October 2026 as Special Executive Magistrates, and on what basis is an ACP treated as 'Superintendent of Police or equivalent'? Its date, signatory, term and powers conferred.
why_it_matters: Read from secondary reproductions, CrPC s.21 had no police-officer clause and BNSS s.15 adds one limited to officers 'not below the rank of Superintendent of Police or equivalent' (LAW-BNSS-007). Reporting calls the Delhi magistrate an ACP (HIST-DEL26-019). In 2018 Delhi ACPs were acting as SEMs under the CrPC and the Delhi Police defended that in the High Court (PROC-DEL-010), and in 2017 the Supreme Court issued notice to all States on misuse of SEM powers (PROC-SC-024). Neither has a ruling in hand. Whether an ACP is 'equivalent' to an SP turns on a notification or a rank-equivalence order that no source read states. The archive does not conclude either way. The claim in circulation that the Supreme Court questioned police SEMs in 2018 is supported only by an unread April 2018 headline. SEARCHED 19 October 2026: no Delhi notification under BNSS s.15, no Gazette entry and no rank-equivalence order for ACPs turned up in any search. The CrPC and BNSS texts are as in LAW-BNSS-007. Absence from a news search is weak evidence. The Tribune (19 Oct) calls the magistrate who extended custody a 'newly appointed Special Executive Magistrate' at Mandir Marg police station (HIST-DEL26-024); a new appointment would have its own notification, which is the document this question asks for.
lawful_route: RTI to the Delhi Government's Home Department and Delhi Police (rtionline.gov.in) for the s.15 notification and any rank-equivalence order; the Delhi Gazette; the Delhi High Court's 2018 PIL file and the Supreme Court's file in Aldanish Rein v. Union of India for orders.

question: The Special Executive Magistrate's order of 19 October 2026 extending the judicial custody of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka by two days: its text, the grounds, the days police asked for, who passed it, and what was decided on Wednesday 21 October, when they are due to be produced again. Were they released, on what bond or surety? And did the magistrate's complaint of threats produce an FIR or only a non-cognisable report?
why_it_matters: Reports on 18 October describe a hearing that passed no order and four sureties rejected, which is the CJP's account. A pre-hearing report of 19 October says the two were due before the magistrate at 2 pm. No report of the outcome has been found. The Daily Jagran says a non-cognisable report was registered over the threats and Neo Politico says an FIR was, so the record on that point conflicts (HIST-DEL26-023). SEARCHED 19 October 2026: no report of the 2 pm hearing's outcome, and no report of a release after 11 October other than the first one. Still open. 19 October 2026 UPDATE: custody was extended by two days on 19 October (HIST-DEL26-024) and the next production is Wednesday 21 October. No report gives the grounds or the days police sought. A forwarded message says police wanted five days because of a feared protest call in the festive season; no report read says that, so it stays unrecorded until an order or a report supports it.
lawful_route: The magistrate's orders of 14 and 18 October; Tihar Jail release records; any petition in the Delhi High Court (the CJP is reported to have consulted counsel).

question: Does the High Powered Enquiry Committee's own notice give the date, the hours and the venue of its sitting on 29 October 2026, and does it say whether the sitting continues on 30 October?
why_it_matters: PROC-SC-025 records the sitting from PTI's report of 24 October 2026, which changed from two days to one within hours. The Committee's own notice would settle the length and would lift the item from REPORTED to VERIFIED. It matters now because the report invites affected persons to walk in on the day, and a person deciding whether to go should be told what the Committee itself says. hpec.nic.in could not be reached from this archive's build environment on 25 October 2026, so the notice was not read. SEARCHED 28 October 2026: hpec.nic.in was still unreachable from this environment, by a direct fetch and by Firecrawl. A news search found no report of the notice. Three outlets still gave the two-day version (see PROC-SC-025). Still open.
lawful_route: Read the public notice on hpec.nic.in (Supreme Court Orders and home pages) from an ordinary connection, or ask the Member Secretary through the contact details on the Committee's site (PROC-SC-017).
